subject: StratusCare MAP: private pool sizing & final-mile lead times
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP and capacity ask — private pool sizing & lead times

Anna / procurement team —

Thanks for the call today. Per our conversation, I’m circulating a draft Mutual Action Plan (attached) that ties together the evaluation milestones, procurement checkpoints, and an initial capacity reservation runway for a private Dedicated GPU pool. High-level ask: can you confirm procurement windows (PO cadence) so we can lock tranches?

Key assumptions we used in the draft MAP:
- Target go-live: Q3 2027 (production traffic by early Aug)
- Initial private pool: 8 H100s (canary tranche) -> expand to 24–32 H100s over 3 tranches
- Lead times: H100 availability estimate 10–14 weeks after order; provisioning private pool nodes ~4–6 weeks post-PO (network & VPC integration adds ~2 weeks)
- Acceptance gating: SOC2 evidence + performance eval (2-week canary, 95th %-tile latency SLO 120ms target for 1k QPS steady-state with batching)

Attachments: stratuscare_map_v3.pdf (MAP with milestones, acceptance criteria), gpu_sizing_sheet.xlsx (raw sizing calc).

Specific asks for StratusCare procurement:
1) Preferred billing: monthly usage + reserved tranche commitment, or full monthly reservation?
2) PO target date for tranche 1 (recommended by 2027-06-14 to meet Aug canary)
3) Contract reviewers and expected redline turnaround (we typically see 3–7 business days for standard SaaS + dedicated infra SOW)

Ben / Neha — can you validate sizing rationale and add notes on fallback (lower-precision quantization options and burst capacity)?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a playbook timeline once procurement dates clear.

—

Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft MAP and capacity ask — tranche pricing + sizing rationale

Naomi / Neha —
Attached: gpu_sizing_sheet.xlsx (contains per-node delta, expected QPS headroom, and canary cost table). Summary below.

Pricing (sample, per-month reserved):
- 4 H100s (canary): $38,000/mo reserved, burst rate $2.45/hr/node; one-time setup $6,000
- 8 H100s: $72,000/mo reserved, burst rate $2.20/hr/node; one-time setup $8,500
- 16 H100s: $136,000/mo reserved, burst rate $1.95/hr/node; setup $12,000
- 32 H100s: $256,000/mo reserved, burst rate $1.70/hr/node; setup $20,000

Sizing rationale:
- StratusCare target: ~1k steady QPS with 90% of requests short-context (<512 tokens). With batching and KV caching we estimate 8 H100s will handle canary with room for bursts; 16 H100s is recommended for production headroom.
- If procurement prefers 4 H100 canary, plan a soft-canary approach: 4 H100s for a restricted traffic slice (internal + beta customers) for 2 weeks; then step to 8 H100s for broader canary.
- Lead-time note: ordering 4 vs 8 has limited effect on chip procurement timeline; primary delta is queue priority — we can prioritize a smaller tranche for faster allocation, but expect 8–10 weeks min.

Fallbacks to reduce cost quickly:
- Low-precision quantization (4-bit) can reduce per-node inference cost by ~25% at modest accuracy loss for some prompts.
- Hybrid routing: route tail latency-sensitive requests to smaller hosted variant, non-critical bulk to private pool.

I’ll turn this into a clean tranche quote PDF once Naomi confirms we should send it to Anna/procurement.

—

Subject: Onboarding runbook & performance acceptance — proposed canary window

Anna —
Following up with operational details that should be part of the MAP’s acceptance criteria. Hope this helps procurement and SRE to plan.

Proposed onboarding steps (high level):
- Week 0: Contract + PO received; kickoff call; exchange network contacts + initial SSO/KMS requirements
- Week 1–2: VPC peering & firewall rules; service account provisioning; encryption key exchange (customer KMS support available)
- Week 3: Canary tranche deployment (4–8 H100s depending on PO); smoke test with synthetic workload using your eval set
- Week 4: 2-week live canary; run the provided prompt set and run perf/eval; collect token-level cost and latency traces
- Week 6–8: Scale to tranche 2 (add 8–16 nodes), finalize production cutover

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Functional: model responses deterministic within acceptable fuzz, no sensitive config leakage in logs
- Performance: 95th %-tile latency under 120ms for defined prompt set at production concurrency; memory/kv cache utilization within expected bounds
- Security: SOC2 evidence checklist items provided, network flow logs verified, KMS test pass

If StratusCare wants a minimal risk path: we can target a 4-node canary for internal usage for 2 weeks, then scale. That reduces financial commitment but adds an extra tranche.

Operational asks for the MAP: please provide a primary SRE contact and a billing contact so we can include them in the SOW. Also confirm if you require on-prem package (air-gapped) — that changes lead times materially.

Marcus Lin
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

- 2027-06-14: PO received (tranche 1)
- 2027-06-21: SOW & contract countersigned
- 2027-07-05: SOC2 artifact handoff + network onboarding initiation
- 2027-08-02: Canary tranche live (4–8 H100s) and start 2-week canary window
- 2027-08-16: Canary acceptance review; begin tranche 2 provisioning if accepted

If procurement prefers the smaller 4-node canary to accelerate allocation, we can accept that and treat 8-node as tranche 2. Ben will attach the formal tranche quote PDF after I confirm we should send.

Please reply with a simple confirm/adjust for the PO date and preferred initial tranche (4 or 8). If procurement confirms PO by 2027-06-14 we will treat this as the on-ramp timeline and finalize the MAP doc for signatures.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.
